question: What is the primary clinical purpose of inserting a flatus tube?

options.A: To instill large volumes of cleansing solutions into the colon
options.B: To decompress acute gaseous distension in the lower bowel
options.C: To deliver continuous enteral nutrition directly to the rectum
options.D: To measure core body temperature via the rectal mucosa

explanation: A flatus tube is specifically utilized to allow trapped intestinal gas to escape, relieving abdominal distension and discomfort. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why must a flatus tube be left in place for only a limited duration, typically twenty to thirty minutes?

options.A: Peristaltic waves will naturally expel the device after half an hour
options.B: The tube material degrades rapidly when exposed to lower intestinal enzymes
options.C: Continuous drainage causes severe electrolyte imbalances within minutes
options.D: Prolonged retention can cause mucosal ischemia and damage the rectal wall

explanation: Leaving a rigid or semi-rigid tube in the rectum for too long puts continuous pressure on the delicate mucosal lining, risking ischemia and tissue necrosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which muscular ring guarding the anal canal is under voluntary skeletal control?
explanation: The external anal sphincter is composed of skeletal muscle and is under voluntary conscious control, whereas the internal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: In which direction should a nurse advance a flatus tube to match the anatomical path of the rectum?

options.A: Straight upward toward the umbilicus to bypass the sigmoid colon
options.B: Perpendicular to the pelvic floor to force open the internal sphincter
options.C: Anteriorly toward the pubic symphysis to avoid the rectal valves
options.D: Following the natural posterior curve of the sacrum and coccyx

explanation: The rectum naturally curves along the sacrum and coccyx, so advancing the tube in this posterior trajectory prevents trauma to the anterior rectal wall. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for flatus tube insertion?

options.A: Mild chronic constipation with infrequent bowel movements
options.C: A history of controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes
options.D: Recent rectal or colonic surgical anastomoses

explanation: Introducing a tube near a fresh surgical join in the bowel can disrupt suture lines, leading to dehiscence, leakage, and severe peritonitis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h3)

question: A patient recovering from a low anterior resection of the colon is complaining of severe gas pains and abdominal bloating on the second postoperative day. What is the most appropriate nursing action regarding a flatus tube?

options.A: Proceed with immediate insertion since postoperative gas pain is a primary indication
options.B: Insert the tube immediately but advance it past the sigmoid colon for better results
options.C: Withhold the procedure and consult the surgeon due to the risk of disrupting the suture line
options.D: Administer a cleansing enema instead to encourage natural expulsion of the trapped gas

explanation: Recent bowel surgery involving an anastomosis makes rectal instrumentation hazardous, requiring medical clearance or alternative interventions. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h3)

question: What type of lubricant must be used when preparing a flatus tube for insertion?
explanation: Water-soluble lubricants are necessary because they reduce friction without damaging latex equipment or irritating the sensitive rectal mucosa, and they are easily absorbed or washed away. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why is a waterproof pad placed beneath the patient prior to inserting a flatus tube?

options.A: To provide a sterile field for laying out the clean disposable gloves
options.B: To protect the bed linens from accidental discharge of fecal matter or mucus
options.C: To elevate the patient's hips and straighten the rectosigmoid junction
options.D: To absorb any excess water-soluble lubricant spilled during preparation

explanation: Decompression often releases liquid stool or mucus along with gas, making bed protection necessary for hygiene and patient dignity. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which patient position is standard for the insertion of a flatus tube?
explanation: The left lateral Sims position aligns with the natural anatomical downward curve of the sigmoid colon and rectum, facilitating smooth tube passage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary physiological benefit of instructing the patient to take slow, deep breaths during tube insertion?

options.A: It closes the glottis to reduce patient anxiety and heart rate
options.B: It promotes relaxation of the voluntary and involuntary anal sphincters
options.C: It increases intra-abdominal pressure to help push the gas outward
options.D: It prevents the accidental aspiration of lower intestinal contents

explanation: Deep breathing helps relax abdominal and pelvic floor muscles, making sphincter entry smoother and less painful for the patient. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What immediate action must a nurse take if resistance is encountered while advancing a flatus tube?

options.A: Advance the tube more rapidly to overcome the tight anal sphincter
options.B: Apply gentle rotating pressure to push past the obstructing fecal mass
options.C: Stop advancement immediately to prevent mucosal injury or perforation
options.D: Instill sterile water through the lumen to wash away the obstruction

explanation: Forcing a rectal tube against resistance can cause severe trauma, bleeding, or perforation of the bowel wall. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h6)

question: Approximately how far should a flatus tube be inserted into an adult patient?
explanation: An insertion depth of 10 to 15 centimeters ensures the tip passes through the anal canal and enters the lower rectum where gas pools. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h6)

question: What physical assessment finding best indicates that the flatus tube is successfully decompressing the bowel?

options.A: Complete relaxation of the patient's external anal sphincter
options.B: A decrease in abdominal distension and softness upon palpation
options.C: An immediate increase in bowel sounds across all four quadrants
options.D: A sudden spike in the patient's peripheral blood pressure

explanation: Successful decompression relieves trapped gas, leading to a softer, less distended abdomen and relief from cramping pain. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h7)

question: Why is early ambulation encouraged for surgical patients after the removal of a flatus tube?

options.A: To stimulate natural peristalsis and prevent future gas accumulation
options.B: To prevent the development of deep vein thrombosis in the lower limbs
options.C: To check if the anal sphincter regained normal voluntary tone
options.D: To clear any remaining water-soluble lubricant from the rectum

explanation: Physical activity and movement help activate the gastrointestinal tract, encouraging normal motility and the natural expulsion of gas. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h7)

question: Which unexpected response can be triggered by rectal manipulation during flatus tube insertion?

options.A: Sudden hypertensive crisis due to severe systemic pain
options.B: Hyperactive bowel sounds and immediate projectile vomiting
options.C: Vasovagal response leading to bradycardia and dizziness
options.D: Reflex paralysis of the diaphragm causing respiratory arrest

explanation: The rectum is rich in vagal nerve endings; mechanical stimulation can occasionally trigger a parasympathetic response causing a drop in heart rate and blood pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h8)

question: What is the primary danger associated with leaving a flatus tube in place for an extended period?

options.A: Complete blockage of the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Pressure necrosis and mucosal ulceration of the rectal wall
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the voluntary external anal sphincter
options.D: Rapid dehydration through excessive fluid loss via the tube

explanation: Continuous mechanical pressure from a rigid or semi-rigid tube restricts blood flow to the rectal mucosa, causing ischemia and tissue breakdown. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h8)

question: Which detail is essential to include when documenting a flatus tube procedure in the patient record?

options.A: The exact names of all nursing staff present in the ward
options.B: The brand name and manufacturer of the water-soluble lubricant
options.C: The patient's personal opinion regarding the hospital meal plan
options.D: The size of the tube used and the duration it remained in place

explanation: Documentation must reflect clinical safety parameters, including equipment specifications and retention time, to ensure safe follow-up care. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h9)

question: A nurse notes bright red blood on the tip of the flatus tube immediately after its removal. What is the most critical immediate action?

options.A: Administer an oral coagulant medication without checking vital signs
options.B: Document the finding as a normal expected outcome and discharge the patient
options.C: Notify the physician promptly and document the observation thoroughly
options.D: Reinsert the tube to apply direct pressure against the bleeding site

explanation: Frank rectal bleeding indicates mucosal trauma and requires medical evaluation, close monitoring, and clear documentation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h9)
